THE EVIDENCE

What winning teams actually did

Verified results, documented engineering, and lessons to test in 2027.

2026Hardware · 1st

FAMU–FSU

ECE 301 + MAE 527 · one integrated system

DOCUMENTED

Four subteams owned drivetrain/integration, task mechanisms, navigation/mapping and drone functions. They used separate mechanisms for individual tasks, emphasizing simple physical designs.

University project record

Emergency backups and planned task timing supported the run. Venue lighting caused false LED readings: exposure changes alone were insufficient, so they blocked ambient light. The university reports a late score improvement from 205 to 270.

University competition report
OUR 2027 EXPERIMENT

Test sensing across venue-like lighting before travel. Give tire exchange a simple dedicated mechanism, an owner and an early integration date.

Software evidence & limits

The team repository documents modular ROS2 nodes, LiDAR, Raspberry Pi 4 coordination and Arduino Mega actuator control. This historical stack is not a 2027 requirement. The university does not explicitly label Main/Open. Late changes are reported events; our readiness should not depend on them.

Team repository
2024Hardware · 1st

Clemson · ROAR-E

The clearest public technical record

DOCUMENTED

The team poster describes a conditional state machine, three Pico controllers over I²C, encoder distance measurement and an eight-element line array. Rear traction wheels, front omni wheels and a flexible chassis supported wheel contact and motion.

Team technical poster

They separated power and signal wiring after electrical interference caused unexpected behavior, and distributed servo power across converters. The college describes development across the academic year.

Clemson college result
OUR 2027 EXPERIMENT

Use explicit mission states. Test electrical interference under motor loads, traction and stopping precision. Their wall-alignment tactic belonged to 2024; 2027 clean-lap points require contact-free corrections.

Keep years and categories straight

These are the 2024 robot's methods, not evidence about Clemson 2025. The cited Clemson sources do not explicitly label the bracket. Virginia Tech separately reports the 2024 Open hardware win.

An eight-team elimination bracket follows. Seek direct qualification, then three successive wins. Confirm category format and elimination ties.

Robot, tools, spares, allowed batteries, offline software, manifest and references are packed. Restore a backup or spare and complete three missions within 30 minutes in a drill. Prioritize operational defects in remaining time.

Independent video scoring agrees with local telemetry. Put the next sprint into the largest measured point losses. Twenty demos are development evidence, not proof of tournament reliability.

RELEASE ACCEPTANCE

Consistency beats one perfect demo.

150 sP95 full mission including parking
170 sMaximum each acceptance run
100 / 100Clean frozen-build missions: floor
300 / 300Championship stretch if feasible

Every intended task, legal start, clean laps, genuine exchange, assigned stop/park, flag and safe idle. Publicity is separate.

What the confidence numbers mean

Zero failures in n independent trials give the one-sided 95% exact lower bound 0.05^(1/n): 97.05% at 100/100 and 99.01% at 300/300. This covers sampled conditions, not every venue.

Independent 95% per-run success gives 85.7% probability of three clean elimination runs; 99% gives 97.0%. Correlated venue failures invalidate independence. A clean run can still lose.

Retain the entire configuration-specific dataset. With failures, calculate an exact bound on all results. Report minimum/median/P10 score and median/P95 time with a documented quantile method.

The provisional robot and mission

Evaluate an encoder-equipped differential drivetrain first. Compare alternatives against measured traction, stopping and pit/turn clearance. Use a simple tire mechanism, adjustable sensing mounts and separate mission and motor-control responsibilities.

Use feedback from field features, encoders and obstacle clearance. Timed motion alone is a weak hypothesis for varied construction. Account for tire payload and deployed flag before choosing the footprint.

Armed & stillLegal start + assignmentLap 1Assigned pit + dwellDistinct tire exchangeLap 2Final lap + flagFinish + assigned parkSafe idle

Verify exchange timing, dwell and post-finish parking through Q&A before settling the sequence. Guard transitions, count laps independently and bound retries.

Test protocol, run record and weekly review
  1. Record build, hardware, rules and intended score. Declare formal, stress, comparison or diagnostic before starting.
  2. Independent reset/randomization, balanced assignments and varied legal layouts. Include cold boots and valid battery variation.
  3. Permitted setup actions only. Video referee-style starts and score tasks independently.
  4. Keep every started attempt. Compare video scoring with onboard telemetry. Log finish, parking and idle separately.
  5. Repeat affected evidence after changes. Keep extreme stress cases separate from the declared match-condition distribution.

R19: telemetry stays onboard during matches; no off-robot communication except required game interfaces. Retrieve during permitted access afterward; wireless devices off when not competing.

Capture each run

ID/date/operator/scorer · build/hardware/rules · board/layout/assignment/light/battery · boot/start/calibration · legality/cards · laps · pit/dwell/overlap · tire drop location and distinct pickup · contacts per lap · final-lap flag · finish/park/idle times · task/bonus/publicity/deductions · criterion · video/logs · failure/next experiment/owner.

Test a second board and operator, varied lighting, sensing issues and valid battery states. Explore preview 3–4 obstacles separately from V2 formal scoring. Once integrated, schedule at least 12 balanced full missions/week.

Hold a 30-minute weekly review: gate, build, all attempts, points lost by task, three largest risks, next owned experiment, rule updates and actual capacity. Record decisions, alternatives, prior criteria, matched evidence, costs, risks and retest triggers.

Entry/resources

Confirm category/eligibility, budget and field access by Oct 15.

Geometry/exchange

Prove minimum size, swept turn, pit overlap, pickup and retention before fabrication commitments.

Field dependence

Retire false-start, light sensitivity and drift using altered layouts and another board.

Integration/power

Test shared interfaces, motor interference, cold boots, brownouts and wear early.

Rules/scoring

Capacity/repairs

Reserve lab time, quote lead times, qualify spares and train backup operators.

Planning basis: 4–6 contributors, 24–40 combined hours/week and regular field access. Replace assumptions with committed hours. Reduce work December 18–January 3. Quote field, robot, spare parts, consumables, memberships, registration and travel separately; reserve at least 20% of engineering funds for replacements/contingencies.

Limited capacity calls for standard controllers/fabrication and less novelty while protecting full integration and testing. Missing Jan 14 or Mar 4 is a schedule risk, not a reason to claim confidence from fewer demos.

Submit by internal Feb 15, rehearse limited access/charging, two-minute setup and score review. Inspect all intended configurations. Pack matching spares, tools, mounts, fasteners, offline releases, calibration, manifest, rules and scoring video. Resolve carrier battery rules when travel is booked.

THE STRATEGY TEST

Thirty seconds buys three points.

A fresh-tire pickup alone earns 40. A complete clean-lap sequence earns 75. Protect those tasks first.

+3Saving 30 seconds−40Missing a fresh-tire pickup

An extra 7.5 percentage points of failure on a 40-point task erases a three-point speed gain in expected score. Roughly 0.85 percentage points of additional risk of losing a nominal 355-point run does the same.

Arithmetic examples, not measured probabilities. Elimination survival and the lower tail matter alongside the average. A winning-score threshold has not been established.

Full scoring, penalties and physical constraints
TaskV2 points
Entry / three-lap finish within 180 s / green start25 / 100 / 10
Pit after lap 1 or 2 / assigned spot15 / 15; under 2 s dwell gives 10 generic-stop points
Drop tire / pick up a different fresh tire25 / 40
Assigned final park / final-lap school flag15 / 25
Gray-wall clean / vehicle-obstacle clean10/lap / 15/lap
Publicity / speed10 subject to confirmation / +1 per full 10 s saved

A 120 s finish adds six: nominal 351 without publicity, 361 with it. Contacts lose clean-lap credits. Early start loses green credit, incurs −2 and a Yellow Card (G05). Red Card zeros the score and loses elimination (C03); another Yellow can escalate.

  • R01: robot start maximum 12 × 12 × 12 in. Minimum 10 in long × 10 in wide for first 3 in above surface, noncontracting. One unit. A solid lower prism is not specified.
  • R02/R16: maximum 12 kg; power distribution ≤30 V.
  • R03/R04: five-second stillness after manual start; accessible marked emergency stop.
  • GM2 §3.3: more than 75% inside assigned spot for stop/end credit. Three V2 spots.
  • G02/G08/GS01: ±1 in position tolerance; setup/randomization interaction restrictions.
  • C02: scoring questions within ten minutes.
